falsePositiveMechanism.earlyReturn: qa-engine.js:224-227 — !opened returns early (and emits NO_POPUP), so HCM is reachable only when opened is true
falsePositiveMechanism.defect: the second disjunct (headText !== prevHead) was written so an inflected surface whose popup shows a lemma still counts as opened. It is also satisfied by a popup belonging to an unrelated word, provided that word differs from the previous iteration’s headword. For the three Obgleich nodes the popup never showed "Obgleich" (5.1s of polling, P27) yet opened evaluated true, so HCM compared Obgleich’s span colour against another word’s headword colour.
falsePositiveMechanism.desiredInvariant: HCM must compare a span against a headword proven to belong to the same clicked surface, or explicitly establish that a lemma popup is the correct popup for that surface. A popup belonging to an unrelated word must never satisfy opened.

findings: the harness did not reproduce the LOOSE baseline: expected 3/3/3/4/1/1 HCM per chapter (from P26), measured 0/3/0/3/0/0. Selective-index probing cannot reproduce the engine’s sequential state — prevHead is a running value over ALL nodes in engine order, and popup state accumulates across the full pass, so probing three chosen indices produces a different chain.
the STRICT mode eliminated legitimate findings: a1-7 (G1) 3 → 1 and a1-8 (G3) 3 → 0. Under the brief’s success criteria that alone disqualifies it.

freshPopups was 0 or 1 in every chapter, including chapters whose findings are known-genuine. That is the diagnosis of the STRICT design: the .word-pop container is reused and mutated, not recreated, so container-freshness is the wrong ownership signal — it cannot distinguish "re-rendered for me" from "left over from someone else".

successCriteria.1_threeFalsePositivesDisappear: NOT DEMONSTRATED — the harness never reproduced them in LOOSE mode, so their disappearance in STRICT mode proves nothing
successCriteria.3_lemmaInflectionCasesRemainDetectable: NOT TESTED — zero lemma cases (surface ≠ headword) were observed in the six probed chapters, so the very case the loose fallback exists for was never exercised
successCriteria.6_noDependenceOnStalePopupState: FAILED by the tested design — container freshness IS stale-state dependence in disguise

verdict: NOT SAFE TO APPLY. The false-positive mechanism is proven (P27) but this phase’s candidate fix is disproven and the regression is inconclusive by construction.
whatTheNextIterationNeeds: a FULL-PASS diagnostic re-implementation that iterates every node in engine order and maintains prevHead exactly as qa-engine.js does — anything less cannot reproduce the LOOSE baseline and therefore cannot validate a change
ownership by headword ELEMENT identity (capture the .word-pop-de node before the click, require a different node after) rather than container freshness

at least one true lemma case (surface ≠ headword) located first, by scanning the 34 remaining HCM records for headText ≠ surface — if none exists in the corpus, the loose fallback may be dead code and the fix becomes trivial; that scan is cheap and should precede any change
